record.original_question: Can rare intermediate-mass PBHs seed early massive galaxies and supermassive black holes by enhancing local cold-dark-matter growth, thereby explaining scenarios in which supermassive-black-hole formation precedes or is contemporaneous with massive-galaxy formation at epochs earlier than standard structure formation predicts?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a cosmological setting in which a population of primordial black holes (PBHs) — black holes formed in the early universe from the collapse of large overdensities, before any stellar formation — is present in addition to standard cold dark matter (CDM). Assume that a rare subpopulation of these PBHs has masses in the intermediate-mass black hole (IMBH) range, defined as $M_{\mathrm{PBH}} \in [10^{3},10^{6}]\,M_{\odot}$, and that each such PBH acts as a localized overdensity that seeds nonlinear gravitational growth of the surrounding CDM via Bondi-type accretion and gravitational instability.

Within the framework of standard ΛCDM perturbation theory, structure formation proceeds hierarchically and the first supermassive black holes (SMBHs, with $M \in [10^{6},10^{10}]\,M_{\odot}$) and the first massive galaxies emerge at redshifts and abundances determined by the linear power spectrum of Gaussian primordial fluctuations.

Question: Determine whether a cosmologically consistent abundance and mass spectrum of rare IMBH-scale PBHs can:

(i) seed the formation of SMBHs of mass $\gtrsim 10^{6}\,M_{\odot}$ at redshifts $z \gtrsim 7$, by enhancing the local growth of CDM around each PBH so as to overcome the limits set by ΛCDM linear structure formation;

(ii) simultaneously seed the formation of the host massive galaxies of these SMBHs at comparably early epochs; and

(iii) produce a temporal ordering in which SMBH assembly precedes or is contemporaneous with the assembly of the surrounding massive galaxy.

Quantify the required PBH mass function $\psi(M_{\mathrm{PBH}})$ and dark-matter fraction $f_{\mathrm{PBH}} = \Omega_{\mathrm{PBH}}/\Omega_{\mathrm{CDM}}$ that would realize (i)–(iii) while remaining consistent with all existing observational constraints on PBH abundance across the IMBH window.
artifact.category_tag: Primordial black holes and early structure formation
artifact.status_search_result: The question remains an active open problem. Recent 2024–2025 works (e.g., A&A studies on primordial seeding of JWST-observed early black holes, simulations of PBH-seeded halos in the first billion years, and proposals of PBHs as seeds for extremely overmassive AGN) explore the scenario as a viable pathway and provide partial supporting evidence (high BH-to-stellar mass ratios, low-metallicity hosts), but no consensus or definitive demonstration exists; alternative seeding channels (direct collapse, runaway mergers) remain competitive.

status_evidence.title: Exploring a primordial solution for early black holes detected with JWST
status_evidence.snippet: Cosmological primordial black hole seeds present an alternative path for the seeding of early structures and their baryonic contents.
status_evidence.claim: PBH seeding of early SMBHs is being actively explored as a viable but unconfirmed mechanism for JWST observations.

status_evidence.title: The properties of primordially-seeded black holes and their hosts in the first billion years
status_evidence.snippet: Simulations found that intermediate mass primordial black holes could implant themselves in halos containing dense gas and start growing early enough to achieve supermassive black hole status prior to 1 Gyr.
status_evidence.claim: Recent simulations partially support the IMBH-PBH seeding scenario but do not resolve it definitively.

status_evidence.title: Primordial Black Holes as Seeds for Extremely Overmassive AGN Observed by JWST
status_evidence.snippet: PBH models naturally predict high black hole-to-stellar mass ratios and low metallicities for hosts of early AGN.
status_evidence.claim: Active research continues to test PBHs as SMBH seeds; the question is open.

status_evidence.title: Physical Pathways for JWST-observed Supermassive Black Holes in the Early Universe
status_evidence.snippet: Reviews multiple seeding channels (direct collapse, stellar, primordial) for early SMBHs.
status_evidence.claim: Multiple competing seeding pathways remain under consideration, indicating no settled answer.
